title: Hippo Signaling Pathway Involvement in Osteopotential Regulation of Murine Bone Marrow Cells Under Simulated Microgravity.
authors: Tyrina, Ekaterina; Yakubets, Danila; Markina, Elena; Buravkova, Ludmila
one_liner_zh: 该文研究模拟微重力下Hippo信号通路对骨髓细胞成骨分化的影响，涉及Yap1和Runx2转录因子，但无蛋白质-DNA互作建模、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The development of osteopenia is one of the most noticeable manifestations of the adverse effects of space factors on crew members. The Hippo signaling pathway has been shown to play a central role in regulating the functional activity of cells through their response to mechanical stimuli. In the present study, the components of the Hippo pathway and the protective properties of osteodifferentiation inducers were investigated under simulated microgravity (smg) using a heterotypic bone marrow cell culture model, which allows for the maintenance of the close interaction between the stromal and hematopoietic compartments, present in vivo and of great importance for both the fate of osteoprogenitors and hematopoiesis. After 14 days of smg, the osteopotential and osteodifferentiation of bone marrow stromal progenitor cells, the expression of Hippo cascade genes and the immunocytochemical status of the adherent fraction of bone marrow cells, as well as the paracrine profile in the conditioned medium and the localization of Yap1 and Runx2 in mechanosensitive cells of the bone marrow were obtained. Simulated microgravity negatively affects stromal and hematopoietic cells when interacting in a heterotypic murine bone marrow cell culture. This is evidenced by the decrease in cell proliferation and osteopotential. Changes in the production of pleiotropic cytokines IL-6, GRObeta and MCP-1 were revealed. Fourteen days of simulated microgravity induced a decrease in the nuclear translocation of Yap1 and the transcription factor Runx2 in the stromal cells of the intact group. Exposure to osteogenic induction conditions partially compensated for the negative effect of simulated microgravity. The data obtained will be crucial for understanding the effects of spaceflight on osteoprogenitor cell growth and differentiation via Hippo-Yap signaling.
abstract_zh: 骨质减少的发展是太空因素对乘员不良影响最显著的表现之一。Hippo信号通路已被证明在通过细胞对机械刺激的响应来调节其功能活性中发挥核心作用。在本研究中，利用异型骨髓细胞培养模型，在模拟微重力（smg）条件下研究了Hippo通路的组成部分及成骨分化诱导剂的保护特性，该模型能够维持体内存在的基质与造血区室之间的紧密相互作用，这种相互作用对骨祖细胞的命运和造血功能均至关重要。经过14天的smg处理后，获得了骨髓基质祖细胞的成骨潜能和成骨分化、Hippo级联基因的表达及骨髓细胞贴壁部分的免疫细胞化学状态，以及条件培养基中的旁分泌谱和骨髓机械敏感细胞中Yap1和Runx2的定位。模拟微重力在异型小鼠骨髓细胞培养中相互作用时对基质细胞和造血细胞产生负面影响。这通过细胞增殖和成骨潜能的下降得以证实。还揭示了多效性细胞因子IL-6、GRObeta和MCP-1产生的变化。十四天的模拟微重力诱导了完整组基质细胞中Yap1和转录因子Runx2核转位的减少。成骨诱导条件的暴露部分补偿了模拟微重力的负面影响。所获得的数据对于理解太空飞行通过Hippo-Yap信号对骨祖细胞生长和分化的影响至关重要。
